def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers_list = instance["customer_ids"]
    customers = set(customers_list)
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]

    # ---------- Helpers ----------
    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for v in route:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            c += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return c

    def try_merge(routes, where, i, j, i_at_end, j_at_end):
        # routes are represented as lists without depot.
        # where[v] = (ridx, pos_index) where pos is 0..len-1.
        ri, pi = where[i]
        rj, pj = where[j]
        if ri == rj:
            return False
        r1 = routes[ri]
        r2 = routes[rj]

        cap1 = 0
        for v in r1:
            cap1 += demands[v]
        cap2 = 0
        for v in r2:
            cap2 += demands[v]
        if cap1 + cap2 > capacity:
            return False

        # Only allow connecting ends
        if i_at_end == "tail" and pi != len(r1) - 1:
            return False
        if i_at_end == "head" and pi != 0:
            return False
        if j_at_end == "head" and pj != 0:
            return False
        if j_at_end == "tail" and pj != len(r2) - 1:
            return False

        # Determine concatenation direction
        # Case 1: i is tail of r1 and j is head of r2 => r1 + r2
        # Case 2: i is tail of r1 and j is tail of r2 => r1 + reversed(r2)
        # Case 3: i is head of r1 and j is head of r2 => reversed(r1) + r2
        # Case 4: i is head of r1 and j is tail of r2 => reversed(r1) + reversed(r2)
        if i_at_end == "tail" and j_at_end == "head":
            new_route = r1 + r2
        elif i_at_end == "tail" and j_at_end == "tail":
            new_route = r1 + r2[::-1]
        elif i_at_end == "head" and j_at_end == "head":
            new_route = r1[::-1] + r2
        else:  # head-tail
            new_route = r1[::-1] + r2[::-1]

        # Update structures
        routes[ri] = new_route
        routes[rj] = None
        for idx in range(len(new_route)):
            where[new_route[idx]] = (ri, idx)

        return True

    def rebuild_after_merges(routes, where):
        # compact routes removing None
        new_routes = []
        remap = {}
        for ridx in range(len(routes)):
            if routes[ridx] is not None:
                remap[ridx] = len(new_routes)
                new_routes.append(routes[ridx])
        for v in list(where.keys()):
            r_old, p = where[v]
